design-code-rules.title: Primary elevation – prevailing material
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Where neighbouring homes share one material, alterations to the primary façade must match that prevailing material.
design-code-rules.guidance-text:
Materials used in exterior work should match, or look similar to, the existing house. Many homes on the Estate have used materials that do not reflect the original homes, which harms the Estate's identity and visual coherence.
Encouraged: The change is justified by better energy performance; High-quality, durable materials; High-quality construction; The change protects the character of the house, for example brick on a street of brick homes; Neighbours can make the same change in future
Discouraged: The façade change does not improve energy performance; The change does not fit the street, for example stone cladding on a street of brick or rendered homes; The change does not protect the character of the house; Poor construction detailing

design-code-rules.guidance-text:
Corner plots give the Estate its green spaces, open aspect and symmetry, and are a key part of its planned layout. Most are managed by the Council, but some are within homeowners' property and have been paved or built on. The code discourages side and roof extensions on corner plots and encourages development to the rear.

Discouraged: No planting; Harm to the street scene; Materials that do not match; Poor construction detailing

design-code-rules.requirement-text: New development should increase biodiversity and, where required, achieve at least 10% biodiversity net gain for the host property.
design-code-rules.guidance-text:
Most of the Estate is already built on, so any remaining sites are small sites suited only to infill. London Plan policy H2 asks boroughs to prepare design codes for small sites. The planned layout, corner plots and gardens are what make the Estate a non-designated heritage asset, and the residents' charter asks for the regular gaps between terraces to be kept.
Encouraged: Scale in proportion to the house and its surroundings; High-quality, durable materials; A contemporary take on the municipal estate character; High-quality construction detailing, such as drainage; Enough private outdoor space kept for the original home; The new home faces the street
Discouraged: A new home not in line with the front of its neighbours; Openings onto the street that do not fit the context or are poor quality; Standard design that ignores the municipal estate character; Not enough outdoor space for the new home and the original home; The new home turns away from the street; New homes on corner plots, which harm the heritage asset
